scope.target: SIS-note confidential-transfer MVP SDK and native CLI surfaces
scope.boundary: Verifier, serializer, digest, Merkle, envelope, and root-window paths operate on public transaction data. Prover and sampler paths handle wallet-local note openings, amounts, bit decompositions, and proof masks. The OCaml, Haskell, and TypeScript implementations are reviewed reference runtimes, not constant-time kernels for hostile shared-process or remote-oracle deployment.

secretData: input and output note amounts before disclosure policy is applied
range bit openings and complement openings
balance, range, and nullifier proof masks
nullifier secret opening material before the public nullifier is derived
publicData: commitments, nullifiers, proofs, Merkle paths, roots, and accepted-root windows
transaction contexts, envelope digests, wallet proof request digests, and proof digests
verifier policies, fee policies, network IDs, asset IDs, and ledger epochs

reviewItems.finding: TypeScript proof-mask helpers use Node.js crypto.randomInt with explicit bound and allocation checks.
OCaml and Haskell samplers read /dev/urandom and use rejection sampling for unbiased bounded integers; rejection timing is independent of wallet secrets but depends on fresh randomness.

Balance, range, and nullifier provers process secret openings and masks in high-level runtimes. They are acceptable only as wallet-local reference paths, not as constant-time services exposed to adversarial timing observers.

Verifier and ledger-step APIs consume public commitments, nullifiers, roots, paths, proofs, fee policies, and spent sets. Data-dependent rejection behavior is therefore not a witness side channel for accepted public transaction data.
Transaction context, envelope, accepted-root-window, wallet-request, and proof digest serializers are domain-separated public encodings with exact-shape and canonical integer checks.

residualRisks.mitigation: Do not deploy the OCaml, Haskell, or TypeScript prover/sampler paths as shared-process or remote proof-generation oracles. A hostile co-residency launch requires a constant-time native prover kernel or an external side-channel signoff for the selected implementation.
residualRisks.launchCondition: External review must sign off on the selected prover/sampler implementation before a production launch claims side-channel hardening.

residualRisks.mitigation: The local manifest documents data classes, reviewed surfaces, and residual assumptions; final launch still requires external cryptography/implementation review.
residualRisks.launchCondition: Set externalReview.status to signed_off only after an external reviewer approves the selected implementation boundary.
